task_2.title: Correct `__attrs_pre_init__` argument forwarding
task_2.description: The update fixes `attrs`-generated initialization so `__attrs_pre_init__` receives the same constructor values that the generated `__init__` received, including explicit values for non-keyword-only attributes that define defaults or factories.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attrs` classes invoking `__attrs_pre_init__` pass through the actual constructor argument values for non-keyword-only attributes, including attributes with defaults or factories, instead of substituting default-derived values when callers supplied explicit input.

expectation.grounded: For `attrs` classes whose generated `__init__` calls `__attrs_pre_init__`, the hook must receive the bound `__init__` parameter values for all forwarded attributes. Non-keyword-only attributes with a declared default or factory must no longer be forwarded to `__attrs_pre_init__` using their default expression or the internal no-value sentinel when the caller explicitly passed a value. Existing keyword-only forwarding semantics should remain aligned with the generated constructor's parameter binding.
expectation.conceptual: Pre-init hooks should see the same inputs that object construction received. If a caller passes a value into an `attrs` class constructor, `__attrs_pre_init__` should observe that value rather than a fallback default.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the generated `__init__` signature, positional versus keyword-only classification, attribute assignment semantics, default or factory behavior when an argument is omitted, or converter and validator execution behavior beyond correcting the values observed by `__attrs_pre_init__`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep normal construction behavior stable and limit the fix to what pre-init hooks observe during initialization.

behavior: Explicit values supplied for non-keyword-only attributes with declared defaults are forwarded into `__attrs_pre_init__` as the caller-provided values.

Explicit values supplied for non-keyword-only attributes backed by factories are forwarded into `__attrs_pre_init__` as the caller-provided values instead of an internal placeholder that represents an omitted argument.

Constructors that mix required attributes, defaulted attributes, factory-backed attributes, keyword-only attributes, and keyword-only defaulted attributes forward a consistent argument set to `__attrs_pre_init__` that matches the generated `__init__` parameter binding.
The change affects the observable inputs to `__attrs_pre_init__` without altering the public constructor shape or subsequent initialization flow.
acceptance_criteria: When an `attrs` class defines `__attrs_pre_init__` and a caller provides an explicit value for a non-keyword-only field with a default, the hook should receive that explicit value.

When an `attrs` class defines `__attrs_pre_init__` and a caller provides an explicit value for a non-keyword-only field with a factory, the hook should receive that explicit value rather than the internal omitted-argument sentinel.
When a class mixes non-keyword-only and keyword-only fields, `__attrs_pre_init__` should receive values for each parameter that match the arguments accepted by the generated constructor.
When a value is not explicitly provided, `__attrs_pre_init__` should continue to observe the same bound constructor parameter value that the generated `__init__` itself received for that parameter.

task_1.title: Align attrs kw_only behavior with dataclasses
task_1.description: attrs 25.4.0 changes how class-level `kw_only=True` is applied so that `attrs.define()` follows dataclass-style behavior: only fields declared on that class become keyword-only unless a field explicitly opts out. The update also adds `force_kw_only` as a compatibility switch for legacy all-fields keyword-only behavior and may expose invalid constructor ordering in some inherited class hierarchies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 25.4.0 preserves the intended constructor behavior for classes using `kw_only=True`, especially when inheritance and field-level `kw_only=False` are involved, while allowing applications that depend on the legacy all-fields keyword-only behavior to opt into compatibility mode.

expectation.grounded: For `attrs.define(kw_only=True)`, only attributes declared on the decorated class should resolve to keyword-only unless a field explicitly sets `kw_only=False`; inherited attributes should keep their existing resolved keyword-only status instead of being forcibly converted. `attrs.field()` and `attr.ib()` should honor an explicit `kw_only=False` even when the class sets `kw_only=True`. `force_kw_only` should be available on both `attrs.define()` and `attr.s()` so callers can restore the legacy behavior where `kw_only=True` forces both local and inherited attributes to become keyword-only. Upgrades must account for the fact that constructor generation can now fail for hierarchies where a defaulted positional base attribute ends up before a required positional subclass attribute.
expectation.conceptual: Classes that enable keyword-only mode should now behave like dataclasses: the setting applies to that class's own fields, not automatically to inherited fields, and an individual field can explicitly remain positional. Codebases that relied on the older blanket keyword-only behavior should be able to opt back into it. If the new positional layout reveals an invalid required-after-default ordering across inheritance, that failure should surface instead of being masked.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the meaning of fields that explicitly declare `kw_only=True` or `kw_only=False`. Preserve legacy forced keyword-only behavior when `force_kw_only=True` is used with `kw_only=True`. Keep `attr.s(kw_only=True)` on its legacy compatibility path by default unless the caller explicitly disables forced keyword-only handling. Limit the behavioral change to keyword-only resolution and resulting initializer validity.
constraints.conceptual: Only keyword-only classification and the resulting constructor shape should change. Explicit field intent must still win, and existing applications that need the previous behavior must have a supported compatibility option instead of being forced into the new semantics.

behavior: Under `attrs.define(kw_only=True)`, inherited base-class fields are no longer automatically converted to keyword-only parameters.
A field declared with `attrs.field(..., kw_only=False)` or `attr.ib(..., kw_only=False)` remains positional even when its class sets `kw_only=True`.
For fields that do not explicitly set `kw_only`, the class-level setting determines whether fields declared on that class become keyword-only.
A new `force_kw_only` parameter on `attrs.define()` and `attr.s()` restores the legacy behavior in which `kw_only=True` forces both local and inherited attributes to be keyword-only.

The default compatibility differs by decorator: `attrs.define(kw_only=True)` uses the new dataclass-like behavior by default, while `attr.s(kw_only=True)` keeps the legacy forced keyword-only behavior unless `force_kw_only=False` is specified.

Some class hierarchies that previously imported successfully can now fail during class creation when a base-class field with a default remains positional and a subclass adds a required positional field after it.
acceptance_criteria: When a class uses `attrs.define(kw_only=True)` and declares one normal field plus one field with `kw_only=False`, the normal field should be keyword-only and the opted-out field should remain positional in the generated initializer.

When a subclass uses `attrs.define(kw_only=True)`, inherited fields should keep their previously resolved positional or keyword-only status instead of being reclassified solely because the subclass enables keyword-only mode.
When `force_kw_only=True` is provided together with `kw_only=True`, both inherited and newly declared fields should be treated as keyword-only, matching the legacy behavior.
When `attr.s(kw_only=True)` is used without overriding `force_kw_only`, upgrading to 25.4.0 should preserve the prior all-fields keyword-only behavior.
When the new behavior leaves a defaulted positional base field ahead of a required positional subclass field, class creation should fail rather than generating an invalid initializer.

task_3.title: Add Python 3.14 compatibility for attrs forward references and slotted classes
task_3.description: Upgrading from 25.3.0 to 25.4.0 adds Python 3.14 and PEP 749 compatibility for attrs-managed classes. The update allows forward-referenced annotations to survive class construction and resolve correctly later, while also fixing slotted-class reference handling so Python 3.14 does not retain stale descriptor links or problematic class-reference cycles.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 25.4.0 makes attrs-based models work correctly on Python 3.14 by supporting forward-referenced annotations under PEP 749 and by fixing reference handling for classes created with `slots=True`.

expectation.grounded: On Python 3.14, `attr.s` and `attrs.define` class construction should tolerate annotations that contain forward references, including stringified references and references to types defined later. `attr.resolve_types` and `attrs.resolve_types` should resolve those annotations through `typing.get_type_hints` while honoring the caller's `include_extras` setting. For slotted attrs classes, creating a class with `slots=True` should leave only a weak back-reference from the original class to the generated slotted class via `__attrs_base_of_slotted__`, and slotted-class creation should clear stale descriptor state on runtimes that expose the CPython support needed for that cleanup.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, attrs classes should behave correctly on Python 3.14: forward-referenced annotations should no longer break class creation or later type resolution, and slotted attrs classes should not retain incorrect references that interfere with normal class lifecycle or cleanup.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing attrs behavior on other supported Python versions. Existing `resolve_types` usage must keep resolving field annotations through the public API, with `include_extras` continuing to control whether annotation extras are preserved. Slotted and non-slotted attrs classes should keep their established public behavior aside from the Python 3.14 compatibility fixes.
constraints.conceptual: This should remain a compatibility-focused upgrade: current attrs usage patterns should continue to work as before, with changes limited to correcting Python 3.14 annotation handling and slotted-class reference cleanup.

behavior: On Python 3.14, attrs retrieves class annotations in a forward-reference-preserving form during class construction so unresolved or later-defined types do not fail immediately.

`attr.resolve_types` and `attrs.resolve_types` consistently pass their `include_extras` option through to runtime type-hint resolution, so resolved field types include or exclude extras according to the caller's choice.
When attrs generates a class with `slots=True`, the original class exposes `__attrs_base_of_slotted__` as a weak reference to the generated slotted class instead of keeping a strong class reference.

During slotted-class creation on Python 3.14 runtimes that provide descriptor-clearing support, attrs removes stale descriptor state from the original class so temporary class metadata does not remain attached.
acceptance_criteria: Given Python 3.14 and an attrs class whose field annotation refers to its own class or to a class defined later, when the attrs class is declared, class creation should succeed without requiring the referenced type to already be bound.

Given a Python 3.14 attrs class with forward-referenced annotations, when `resolve_types` is called after the referenced types exist, the affected field types should resolve to the concrete runtime classes.

Given field annotations that use typing extras, when `resolve_types(..., include_extras=true)` is used, the resolved field types should preserve those extras, and when `include_extras=false` is used, they should not.

Given a class transformed into an attrs class with `slots=True`, when the original class object is inspected, it should expose a weak back-reference to the generated slotted class rather than an unnecessary strong reference.

Given Python 3.14 and slotted attrs class creation, when the original class is no longer otherwise retained, attrs should not leave stale descriptor references that create broken reference cycles or interfere with normal cleanup.

task_4.title: Relax deep_mapping validator requirements
task_4.description: attrs 25.4.0 expands `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` so callers can validate only mapping keys or only mapping values, automatically compose validator lists or tuples, and receive an explicit error when neither key nor value validation is configured.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` supports partial deep validation for mappings by allowing callers to validate only keys or only values, while rejecting configurations that provide neither.

expectation.grounded: In attrs 25.4.0, `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` must allow `key_validator` to be omitted when `value_validator` is provided, and allow `value_validator` to be omitted when `key_validator` is provided. If `key_validator`, `value_validator`, or `mapping_validator` is passed as a list or tuple of validators, the API should treat that collection as a composed validator. Calling `deep_mapping()` with both `key_validator` and `value_validator` omitted must raise `ValueError`. During validation, only the configured key and value validators should run for each mapping entry, and `mapping_validator` should still be applied to the top-level mapping when supplied.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to configure deep mapping validation for just keys, just values, or both, without being forced to provide unused validators. The API should still reject a configuration that performs no deep key or value checks at all, and it should accept multiple validators for each validation stage in a single call.

constraints.grounded: Do not require placeholder validators for unused key or value validation. Do not silently accept a `deep_mapping()` configuration where both `key_validator` and `value_validator` are absent. Preserve observable validation failures from any configured sub-validator, including composed validators created from validator lists or tuples.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must broaden valid configurations without weakening validation guarantees. It should remain impossible to create a deep-mapping validator that skips both key and value checks, and any configured validation step should still fail visibly when its rules are violated.

behavior: `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` now accepts configurations with only `key_validator` or only `value_validator` provided.
When one of the per-entry validators is omitted, validation only runs for the configured side of each mapping entry instead of requiring both sides to be validated.
Calling `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` with neither `key_validator` nor `value_validator` now raises `ValueError` at construction time.
If `key_validator`, `value_validator`, or `mapping_validator` is given as a list or tuple, the validators are combined so all validators in that collection are applied.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller creates `attrs.validators.deep_mapping(value_validator=...)`, it should construct successfully and validate mapping values without requiring a key validator.
When a caller creates `attrs.validators.deep_mapping(key_validator=...)`, it should construct successfully and validate mapping keys without requiring a value validator.
When a caller creates `attrs.validators.deep_mapping()` without both `key_validator` and `value_validator`, it should raise `ValueError` immediately.
When a caller passes a list or tuple of validators for `key_validator`, `value_validator`, or `mapping_validator`, all validators in that collection should be enforced during normal validation.

task_5.title: Expand attrs deep validators to accept validator collections
task_5.description: The upgrade extends attrs deep validation helpers so callers can pass multiple validators as lists or tuples and have them applied together. It also broadens deep mapping validation to support validating only keys or only values, while rejecting an empty deep_mapping configuration that provides neither.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs deep iterable and deep mapping validators accept grouped validators in addition to single validators, and that deep mapping supports key-only or value-only validation while rejecting configurations that specify neither key nor value validation.

expectation.grounded: attrs.validators.deep_iterable() must accept either a single callable validator or a list/tuple of validators for member_validator and iterable_validator. attrs.validators.deep_mapping() must accept either a single callable validator or a list/tuple of validators for key_validator, value_validator, and mapping_validator. When a list or tuple is supplied, it must behave as a combined validator equivalent to applying attrs.validators.and_() to the provided validators. attrs.validators.deep_mapping() must allow key_validator or value_validator to be omitted individually, skip validation for the omitted side, and raise ValueError if both key_validator and value_validator are omitted.
expectation.conceptual: The deep validation helpers should let callers express multiple checks per collection element or mapping layer without manually composing them first. Deep mapping should also support scenarios where only keys or only values need validation, but it should reject being configured with no key or value validation at all.

constraints.grounded: Existing single-validator usage for attrs.validators.deep_iterable() and attrs.validators.deep_mapping() must remain valid. Any supplied mapping_validator remains optional and should only run when provided. Validation failures from supplied sub-validators must continue to surface as validator failures, including TypeError where those validators already do so. Omitting key_validator must not disable value validation, and omitting value_validator must not disable key validation.
constraints.conceptual: Current valid deep-validator usage should continue to work unchanged. The new grouped-validator support must be additive rather than replacing existing behavior, and partial deep mapping validation must only skip the part the caller left unspecified.

behavior: attrs.validators.deep_iterable() now accepts a list or tuple for member_validator and applies all supplied member validators to each iterable element.
attrs.validators.deep_iterable() now accepts a list or tuple for iterable_validator and applies all supplied validators to the outer iterable.
attrs.validators.deep_mapping() now accepts a list or tuple for key_validator, value_validator, and mapping_validator, applying all supplied validators for each respective target.
attrs.validators.deep_mapping() now allows callers to validate only mapping keys or only mapping values by leaving the other validator unset.
attrs.validators.deep_mapping() raises ValueError when created without either a key_validator or a value_validator.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller passes a list or tuple of validators to attrs.validators.deep_iterable() for member_validator, each iterable element should be checked against all of them.
When a caller passes a list or tuple of validators to attrs.validators.deep_iterable() for iterable_validator, the outer iterable should be checked against all of them.

When a caller passes lists or tuples of validators to attrs.validators.deep_mapping(), mapping keys, mapping values, and the mapping itself should each be validated against all validators supplied for that layer.
When attrs.validators.deep_mapping() is configured with only key_validator, it should validate keys and allow values to pass without deep value validation.
When attrs.validators.deep_mapping() is configured with only value_validator, it should validate values and allow keys to pass without deep key validation.
When attrs.validators.deep_mapping() is called without both key_validator and value_validator, it should fail immediately with ValueError instead of creating a validator.

task_7.title: Broaden tuple converter typing for attrs.field
task_7.description: The upgrade corrects the public type annotations for `attrs.field(converter=...)` so tuple-based converter declarations are treated as variable-length tuples rather than single-element tuples. This removes false-positive type-checking failures for valid uses of multiple converters while preserving runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attrs.field(converter=...)` accepts tuple-based converter declarations with any number of converters in the library's public type surface, so valid multi-converter usage does not trigger incorrect static type errors.

expectation.grounded: The public annotations for `attrs.field(converter=...)` should allow `converter` to be supplied as a single converter, a list of converters, or a tuple containing one or more converters. Tuple annotations must represent variable-length tuples of valid converter entries rather than a tuple constrained to exactly one element. Static type consumers should no longer be warned or rejected solely because `converter` is a tuple with multiple converter callables.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare multiple converters in tuple form for `attrs.field()` without type checkers flagging that usage as invalid. The upgrade should align the typing contract with the documented and intended API shape while leaving runtime behavior unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the runtime semantics of `attrs.field()` or narrow currently supported converter forms. Existing accepted converter inputs other than multi-element tuples must remain valid, and the change should be limited to the observable typing contract exposed to users.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove incorrect type-checking friction without altering how converter handling works at runtime or breaking already valid converter declarations.

behavior: The type contract for `attrs.field(converter=...)` now treats tuple-based converter inputs as tuples of arbitrary length instead of tuples with exactly one converter element.
Static analysis tools that consume the library's public annotations should accept `attrs.field(converter=(converter_a, converter_b))` and other multi-element tuple forms as valid.
Single-converter and list-based converter declarations remain part of the accepted public typing surface.
No runtime behavior change is introduced by this upgrade; the effect is limited to annotations and the resulting static-analysis experience.
acceptance_criteria: When a user defines an `attrs.field()` with `converter` set to a tuple containing multiple valid converters, the library's published type information should describe that usage as valid.
When a user provides a single converter or a list of converters to `attrs.field(converter=...)`, those forms should remain valid under the public typing contract.

Upgrading from 25.3.0 to 25.4.0 should not change runtime outcomes for `attrs.field()` usage; the observable change should be the removal of false-positive typing errors for multi-element tuple converters.

task_6.title: Add experimental attrs class inspection API
task_6.description: attrs 25.4.0 adds an experimental public inspection API for attrs-decorated classes. Consumers can now retrieve the effective class-construction properties that attrs resolved after applying defaults, auto-detection, and decorator interactions, including generated methods, hashing mode, keyword-only behavior, pickling support, and class-level hooks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 25.4.0 exposes a public experimental way to inspect the effective construction settings of an attrs-decorated class, so consumers can observe the resolved behavior of the class instead of inferring it from decorator arguments alone.

expectation.grounded: Provide `attrs.inspect(cls)` as a public experimental API that returns an `attrs.ClassProps` instance for a class decorated by attrs. The returned object should report the effective resolved properties used to build the class, including `is_exception`, `is_slotted`, `has_weakref_slot`, `is_frozen`, `kw_only`, `collected_fields_by_mro`, `added_init`, `added_repr`, `added_eq`, `added_ordering`, `hashability`, `added_match_args`, `added_str`, `added_pickling`, `on_setattr_hook`, and `field_transformer`. Hashing state should be represented with `attrs.ClassProps.Hashability`, keyword-only behavior with `attrs.ClassProps.KeywordOnly`, and passing a class that is not attrs-decorated should raise `attrs.exceptions.NotAnAttrsClassError`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to ask attrs how a decorated class was ultimately configured and receive a structured description of the class's final behavior. The inspection result should reflect defaults and automatic decisions that attrs made for the class, including method generation, hashing, keyword-only semantics, match support, pickling support, and relevant class-level hooks. Calling the API on a non-attrs class should fail with the library's dedicated not-an-attrs-class error.

constraints.grounded: The inspection API is observational only and must not change class creation behavior. Reported values must be the effective post-resolution outcomes, not merely raw decorator inputs, including derived hash behavior, cached hashing eligibility, generated-method decisions, pickling generation, and keyword-only mode distinctions between `NO`, `YES`, and `FORCE`. The API is explicitly experimental.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability should expose metadata without altering runtime behavior. It should describe what attrs actually produced for the class, and it should only succeed for classes that were decorated by attrs.

behavior: `attrs.inspect(cls)` is available from the top-level `attrs` package.
Successful inspection returns an `attrs.ClassProps` object representing the effective class-wide construction properties for the inspected attrs class.
`attrs.ClassProps` exposes enum-backed representations for hashing outcomes and keyword-only enforcement through `Hashability` and `KeywordOnly`.
The inspection result reports whether attrs generated initialization, representation, equality, ordering, string conversion, match-args support, and pickling helpers for the class.

The inspection result also reports whether the class is treated as an exception class, whether it is slotted or frozen, whether it has a weak-reference slot, whether field collection followed MRO semantics, and which class-level `on_setattr` and field transformer hooks are effective.
Reported values reflect resolved behavior after applying defaults and auto-detection, including cases where hashing is generated, cached, disabled, or left untouched.
Inspecting a class that is not attrs-decorated raises `NotAnAttrsClassError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer calls `attrs.inspect()` on an attrs-decorated class, it should return an `attrs.ClassProps` object describing the class's effective construction behavior.
When a class relies on decorator defaults or attrs auto-detection, `attrs.inspect()` should expose the resolved outcome rather than only the explicitly supplied decorator arguments.
When hashing behavior is inspected, the result should distinguish between generated hashing, cached generated hashing, explicit unhashability, and leaving hash behavior unchanged.

When keyword-only behavior is inspected, the result should distinguish between no keyword-only enforcement, keyword-only treatment for current-class attributes, and fully forced keyword-only construction.

When attrs-generated methods or features are enabled or suppressed, the inspection result should indicate whether attrs added initialization, representation, equality, ordering, string conversion, match support, and pickling helpers.
When a non-attrs class is passed to `attrs.inspect()`, it should raise `NotAnAttrsClassError` instead of returning inspection data.

task_9.title: Speed up attrs.astuple() for atomic fields
task_9.description: attrs 25.4.0 improves the runtime performance of attrs.astuple() by avoiding unnecessary recursive handling for exact built-in atomic values while preserving existing recursive serialization behavior for attrs instances, collections, mappings, and other non-atomic values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 25.4.0 preserves attrs.astuple() output behavior while delivering the documented runtime improvement for objects that contain atomic built-in values and nested attrs-managed data.

expectation.grounded: attrs.astuple() should treat exact values of NoneType, bool, int, float, str, complex, bytes, ellipsis, type, range, and property as terminal atomic values during recursive conversion and place them into the output unchanged. With recursion enabled, it should continue to recurse into attrs classes and into tuple, list, set, frozenset, and dict values or subclasses using the existing retain_collection_types behavior and existing filter and tuple_factory semantics.
expectation.conceptual: Calling attrs.astuple() after the upgrade should be faster for common scalar-like field values, without changing what callers observe from recursive serialization of attrs objects, collections, mappings, and custom values.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the tuple structure produced by attrs.astuple(), its recurse and filter behavior, or how retain_collection_types affects collection and mapping subclasses. The atomic fast path should apply only to exact built-in atomic types, and non-atomic or user-defined subclass values must continue to follow the pre-existing serialization path.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must not alter serialized results or broaden which values are treated as simple pass-through values beyond the intended built-in atomic cases.

behavior: attrs.astuple() now short-circuits a fixed set of exact built-in atomic value types and emits them directly in the output tuple.
Recursive conversion still traverses nested attrs instances when recurse is enabled.
Collection and mapping values, including subclasses, continue to be recursively converted rather than being treated as atomic.
When retain_collection_types is enabled, collection and mapping subclasses continue to be preserved in the serialized output.
Subclasses of otherwise atomic built-in types are not included in the atomic shortcut and continue through the existing generic serialization behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs.astuple() serializes an attrs instance whose fields are exact built-in atomic values, it should return those values unchanged in the resulting tuple while preserving their runtime value types.
When attrs.astuple() encounters nested attrs instances, collections, or mappings with recursion enabled, it should continue to serialize nested contents according to the existing recursive rules.

When retain_collection_types is true and a field contains a collection or mapping subclass, the serialized result should preserve that container type instead of collapsing it to the default list or dict type.

When a field contains a user-defined subclass of an otherwise atomic built-in type, attrs.astuple() should not treat it as an atomic shortcut case and should preserve prior observable serialization behavior for that value.

task_10.title: Broaden typing for attrs.validators.or_
task_10.description: The 25.4.0 update refines the static typing contract for attrs so that attrs.validators.or_() can combine different validator kinds without producing false type-checker failures. This is a typing compatibility improvement, aimed especially at Pyright, and does not change runtime validation behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs users can combine different validator types with attrs.validators.or_() without false static type errors when modeling fields that accept multiple value types.

expectation.grounded: The public typing for attrs.validators.or_() should accept heterogeneous validators, including combinations such as numeric comparison validators and type-instance validators, when used as the validator argument to attrs.field on attrs classes. A union-typed attribute validated through attrs.validators.or_() should be accepted by static type checkers, including Pyright, as a supported attrs pattern.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to express "value may be one of several types, each with its own validator" through attrs.validators.or_() and have that pattern type-check cleanly without checker-specific workarounds.

constraints.grounded: This is a typing-only compatibility change. It must not alter the runtime semantics of attrs.validators.or_(), existing validator execution, or existing attrs.field and attrs.define usage. Existing validator combinations that already type-check should remain valid.
constraints.conceptual: Upgrading should improve static-analysis acceptance of mixed validator combinations without changing how validation behaves at runtime or breaking existing attrs models.

behavior: attrs.validators.or_() is treated as accepting different validator types within a single combined validator instead of requiring all validators to share one inferred validator type.
An attrs attribute annotated with a union type can use attrs.validators.or_() to combine validators that correspond to different branches of that union and still type-check successfully.
The change affects static typing compatibility, especially for Pyright, rather than observable runtime validation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs field accepts more than one value type, using attrs.validators.or_() with validators appropriate to those different types should not trigger a static typing error caused solely by mixing validator kinds.
When the same mixed-validator attrs pattern is analyzed by Pyright, it should be recognized as valid attrs usage rather than rejected because of the or_() type annotation.
When applications upgrade to 25.4.0, existing runtime validation through attrs.validators.or_() should continue to behave the same as before.

task_8.title: Optimize attrs.asdict() for common values
task_8.description: Upgrade to attrs 25.4.0 so attrs.asdict() is materially faster in common cases while preserving the observable serialization contract for attrs instances, collections, mappings, serializer hooks, and custom subclasses.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 25.4.0 makes `attrs.asdict()` faster for common object graphs without changing the user-visible recursive serialization behavior of attrs instances, collections, mappings, serializer hooks, or subclass handling.

expectation.grounded: With `attrs.asdict()` and `recurse=True`, values whose exact runtime type is `NoneType`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, `str`, `complex`, `bytes`, `EllipsisType`, `type`, `range`, or `property` should be treated as atomic pass-through values in the fast path. Attrs-decorated instances must still recurse through `attrs.asdict()`, collection and mapping values must still be traversed from their runtime type, `retain_collection_types` and `dict_factory` must continue to govern output container construction, and `value_serializer` must remain observable for attribute values and nested non-container values. Instances that merely subclass one of the atomic built-ins must not be treated as exact-type atomic values.
expectation.conceptual: Common scalar values should serialize more quickly, but the serialized result should remain consistent with previous releases. Recursive serialization should still walk attrs objects, containers, and mappings correctly, keep honoring serializer hooks and container options, and avoid changing the behavior of user-defined subclasses just because they inherit from built-in scalar types.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the logical output shape of `attrs.asdict()`. Recursive traversal must continue to honor `recurse`, `retain_collection_types`, and `dict_factory`; mapping keys and values must still be serialized recursively; collection subclasses must still be recognized from their runtime type; and exact-type atomic shortcuts must not broaden to subclasses of those built-ins.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this as a performance-only upgrade in terms of output correctness: speed may improve, but callers should not have to change how they interpret serialized data or how they use existing options and hooks.

behavior: `attrs.asdict()` now short-circuits common exact built-in scalar and descriptor-like values as atomic during recursive serialization.
Recursive serialization of nested attrs instances remains intact and still uses `attrs.asdict()` for those objects.

Collection and mapping values, including subclasses identified from their runtime type, continue to be traversed recursively and reconstructed according to `retain_collection_types` and `dict_factory`.
Custom subclasses of atomic built-ins are not promoted into the atomic fast path solely by inheritance and therefore continue through the normal serialization path.
When `value_serializer` is provided, serialized attribute values and nested non-container values remain subject to serializer-produced output.
acceptance_criteria: When `attrs.asdict()` serializes an attrs instance whose fields contain only exact built-in scalar values such as `None`, booleans, numbers, strings, bytes, `Ellipsis`, `range`, `type`, or `property`, it should return the same logical mapping as before while benefiting from the 25.4.0 common-case speedup.
When an attrs field contains another attrs-decorated instance and `recurse=True`, it should still be serialized recursively rather than left as the original object.
When an attrs field contains collection or mapping subclasses, serialization should still recurse into their contents and respect `retain_collection_types` and `dict_factory` for the produced output.
When a value is a subclass instance of an otherwise atomic built-in type, serialization should not treat it as an exact-type atomic shortcut solely because of that inheritance.
When `value_serializer` is supplied, top-level attribute values and nested non-container values should still reflect the serializer's returned values.
